editorial.verdict: The HD1000 is the entry HD: an aluminum-bodied 14-stitch mechanical with a 4-step buttonhole that owners rate as a solid beginner machine rather than a heavy-fabric tool.
editorial.whoFor: A first-machine buyer who wants Janome's metal body and 25-year warranty and will mostly sew garments, mending and the occasional denim hem.
editorial.skipIf: You want a one-step buttonhole, adjustable presser foot pressure, or you plan to sew bags, webbing or leather regularly.
editorial.keySpec: 860 spm · 14 stitches · 5 mm zigzag · 16.8 lb aluminum body

checks.title: White or Black Edition
checks.body: The HD1000BE is a separate SKU with its own bundle and price at big-box stores. Confirm which one the listing is; the Home Depot price seen is the Black Edition.

checks.title: Bonus bundles
checks.body: Sewing Machines Plus adds extra bobbins and needles to a 4-foot box. Compare the bare machine price before crediting the bundle.

checks.title: HD1000 or HD3000
checks.body: About $200 more buys 18 stitches, a one-step buttonhole and adjustable pressure. Owners call the gap real but not large.

faqs.q: Is the Janome HD1000 good for beginners?
faqs.a: Owners on PatternReview describe it as a beginner machine with simple mechanical controls. It has 14 stitches, a 4-step buttonhole and a built-in needle threader.

faqs.q: Can the HD1000 sew canvas or leather?
faqs.a: One owner thread reports jeans, canvas and nylon webbing sewn without problems; a bag-making reviewer says it is not meant for heavy materials. Janome does not publish a layer or thickness rating.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the HD1000 and HD3000?
faqs.a: The HD3000 adds 18 stitches, a one-step buttonhole, adjustable presser foot pressure and a 6.5 mm zigzag. The HD1000 has 14 stitches, a 4-step buttonhole and a 5 mm zigzag.

faqs.q: How fast does the HD1000 sew?
faqs.a: Dealer spec copy lists 860 stitches per minute.

faqs.q: Does the HD1000 have a free arm and drop feed?
faqs.a: Yes, per the Sewing Machines Plus listing.

faqs.q: How much does the HD1000 weigh?
faqs.a: A directory listing gives 7.6 kg, about 16.8 lb. Janome's US page did not show a weight in the results captured.

faqs.q: What is the HD1000 Black Edition?
faqs.a: A black-bodied version, HD1000BE, sold as a separate SKU with its own bundle. The Home Depot listed it at $403.83.

faqs.q: What warranty does the HD1000 carry?
faqs.a: Janome America states 25 years on materials and workmanship, 5 years electrical and 1 year labor for home use.
